title: The Day Before Yesterday I Slept in the Meadow...
text:
The day before yesterday I slept in the meadow

upon the scent of grass,

yesterday among the pine groves,

today in the quiet forest,

tomorrow, plain with plain,

alone between sky and earth.

The dawn of each sun

reveals a new field to me,

and the dream of each night

the same deep stars.

By day one travels

what by night one dreams:

always the same hope

beneath a different promise,

and at night one keeps watch

over everything the step leaves behind,

military company

on the road of absence.

How much will be what advances,

and how much what returns?

Adventurous heart:

what do you see in what you dream?

Blood, all the blood.

Earth, all your earth.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's march through meadow, pine, forest, dream, blood, and homeland.

title: Poem LXXIII
text:
And that light?

-It is your shadow.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Loynaz's miniature reversal of light and shadow.

title: In Every Grain of Sand...
text: In every grain of sand there is a mountain's collapse.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the aphorism's compression from mountain to grain.

title: The Dry Leaves, Do They Fly or Fall?...
text: The dry leaves, do they fly or fall? Or is it that in every flight the earth remains waiting, and in every fall there is a shiver of wing?
editorial_note: The translation keeps Loynaz's question balanced between falling and flight.

title: The Eyes Look at the Blue Stars...
text:
The eyes look at the blue stars; the feet, humbly beside the ground, uphold a pedestal for the eyes that look at the blue stars.




Nameless Poems, 1953
editorial_note: The translation keeps the prose-poem structure and preserves the source collection note.
